column3: Directly joins the same two groups to refusal after the bayyinah; establishes the evidentiary setting.
Completes the immediate written-source setting, but adds less than 98:1 and 98:4.
Parallels kafaru with a superlative sharr designation, clarifying the evaluative ranking.
Combines Jahannam and khalidin with grouped rejecters; supports the final-state wording.
Sets the commanded din and practices immediately before the focus verdict.
Extends khalidin with an explicit qualification; a boundary for permanence language.
Links disobedience after messenger-delivery to Jahannam and khalidin; includes a boundary route.
The direct khayr al-bariyyah counterpart defines the ranking as response-based.
Connects kufr, false purposelessness, and fire, but only indirectly addresses the focus verdict.
Names Ahl al-Kitab and mushrikun together in resistance to descending khayr.
Supplies the messenger and purified written material that frame the bayyinah.
Fire-directed gathering is only a contrary V12 boundary, not positive support.
Repeats the Jahannam-khalidin formulation, with little additional criterion.
The rewarded khalidin counterpart marks a secondary contrast to the focus outcome.
Fire and khalidin appear with failed worldly protections; partially redundant confirmation.
Adds an entry-into-Jahannam scene without the focus categories or criterion.
Locates Ahl al-Kitab division after the bayyinah, directly sharpening accountability.
Fire imagery is a boundary route only and does not specify the focus judgment.
Calls those gathered to Jahannam worse in place and further astray; a close ranking parallel.
Sets testimony and dissociation from shirk; useful mainly as a contrast boundary.
Restates khalidin and unrelieved punishment without identifying the focus groups.
Fire as created origin is secondary boundary evidence, not the focus fire judgment.
Joins kufr, fire companionship, and khalidin in a distinct denial setting.
Contrasts sharr and rushd without defining the focus ranking or outcome.
A further khalidin repetition, now with absence of protector or helper.
Writing of plotted signs offers only an indirect written-accountability connection.
Names mushrikun and Jahannam with an evil final return; narrower than the focus grouping.
Dissociation from mushrikun is contrast evidence, not a judgment of all such persons.
Names kuffaru min Ahl al-Kitab and overturns assumed security in a historical instance.
Depicts fire's effect but adds no group, criterion, or duration.
Contrasts a God-conscious foundation with collapse into Jahannam; supports moral consequence.
Explicit dissociation from shirk is a boundary, without the focus final verdict.
Khalidin for reward is a secondary outcome contrast and is otherwise redundant.
Portrays kuffar opposing the divine nur, reinforcing resistance to disclosed proof.
Combines fire and khalidin in another accountability scene, though with a qualification.
Affirms the book's descent without doubt; supports the authority of the written evidence.
Uses sharr in a different moral register; preserves a secondary semantic boundary.
The rejected contrary route gives only boundary evidence around the difficult day.
Includes mushrikun in punishment, but lacks the focus's proof and ranking language.
Individual sharr being seen is a limited consequence parallel, not the focus classification.
Generic sharr imagery has no material route to the focus judgment.
Written record and creation language give secondary support for accountable created beings.
Ahl al-Kitab believers receive reward, directly limiting any category-based reading.
Relativizes Ahl al-Kitab possession of favor; supports nonautomatic standing.
Makes revealed writing a binding criterion for Ahl al-Injil, directly relevant to f04.
Reverses who is counted among ashrar; a semantic boundary rather than confirmation.
Presents the believing counterpart with written iman and lasting reward; secondary contrast.
Uses ahl as worthiness for taqwa; only an indirect boundary on group labels.
Shows bayyinat met by kufr and a charge of sihr, a close proof-rejection parallel.
Written-book language is too general after the nearer 98 and 32 evidence.
Names intense fire only; no focus group, response, or ranking.
The rejected fire route serves as contrary boundary evidence only.
Places kuffar beside claimed exemption in writings; supports scrutiny of documentary claims.
Fire's severity and commanded obedience give a secondary consequence-and-duty parallel.
Broad sharr-of-creation language is a boundary to the focused comparative verdict.
False claims to write unseen knowledge form a limited written-authority boundary.
Dissociation from shirk supplies contrast, without the focus's evidentiary sequence.
Direct address to kuffar names the addressees but adds no judgment mechanism.
Pairs kufr and denial of ayat with fire and khalidin; clear but largely redundant.
Contrasts khayr and sharr in human preference, a different evaluative domain.
Repeats kufr, denial of ayat, fire, and khalidin after stronger parallel cards.
Addresses Ahl al-Kitab who reject ayat while witnessing; directly supports proof-based blame.
Fire and khalidin recur with failed wealth and children; redundant to earlier cards.
Rejected fire evidence remains a contrary boundary, not positive interpretive support.
Names kuffar as fire fuel but omits the focus's book, shirk, and permanence frame.
Book containing the addressees' dhikr supports the binding-address dimension.
Mushrikun witness their own kufr and remain in fire; a close but narrower parallel.
Human non-khuld supplies only a lexical boundary for khalidin.
Details unending Jahannam without death or relief; strengthens the outcome texture.
Generic kuffar-as-fire-companions formulation adds little after closer repetitions.
Kufr when the dhikr arrives, alongside an inviolable book, closely frames rejection of proof.
Dissociation from worship is contrast evidence around shirk, not the focus consequence.
Kuffar obstruct the divine path and are gathered to Jahannam; adds a process link.
Explicit lasting Jahannam for mujrim confirms duration, though it lacks the focus groups.
Fire as recompense for denying ayat with dar al-khuld is a compact outcome-and-cause parallel.
Repeats the false-writing boundary already supplied at rank 56.
Kufr and denial of ayat lead to al-jahim; confirms the rejection-to-fire pattern.
Kuffar rushing toward the messenger gives a limited response-to-message parallel.
Ahl al-Kitab belief and taqwa lead to gardens, directly preserving the favorable countercase.
The nafs and su' are a broad moral boundary, not the focus comparative judgment.
Repeats the denial-of-ayat to jahim pattern after the stronger 5:10 card.
Rewarded khalidin is a remote counterpart with no book or rejection criterion.
Opposing God and messenger leads to Jahannam and khalidin; clear consequence parallel.
Sharr and khayr occur in a specific social test, preserving a semantic boundary.
Kufr, movement to darkness, fire, and khalidin provide a secondary outcome contrast.
Evil plotting returning to its people is an indirect accountability parallel.
Sorting vile from good and placing the vile in Jahannam supports evaluative separation.
Clear-book language is too general to add beyond nearer written-evidence cards.
Ahl al-Kitab appears in a historical conflict without the focus's proof or final judgment.
The rejected rescue-from-fire route is contrary boundary evidence only.
Kuffar's later iman not benefiting them sharpens the consequence of delayed response.
The claim of being made enduring by wealth is a narrow lexical contrast to khalidin.
Al-kitab al-mubin is general written-evidence support, already well covered.
Book confirmation and prior scriptures give only indirect support for Ahl al-Kitab accountability.
Doubt and play lack a direct group, outcome, or exact-route contribution.
Jahannam, khalidin, and arrogance add a distinct character marker to the final outcome.
Inheritance provisions have no material connection to the focus readings.
Disbelief alongside entry into fire shows proximity to righteous people is not protective.
Turning from the divine path and fire punishment is a limited consequence parallel.
Lasting punishment and loss give only a broad final-accountability parallel.
Earning al-sayyi'ah and being encompassed by it leads to fire companionship and khalidin.
Supplies the preceding kufr-and-death condition for the nearby 2:162 permanence passage.
States non-exit from fire, adding a direct boundary on the outcome's continuance.
Links reversal after iman to nullified works, fire companionship, and khalidin.
Addresses kuffar with gathering toward Jahannam, a direct collective outcome parallel.
Defines the fire as prepared for al-kafirin; concise outcome confirmation.
Kufr in ayat is paired with fire, including repeated renewal of its consequence.
Defines a form of kufr through differentiating between Allah and messengers.
Calls the preceding group the true kuffar and fixes a prepared humiliating punishment.
Combines Ahl al-Kitab discourse, shirk, forbidden garden, and fire; a decisive category boundary.
Denial of ayat and arrogance lead to fire companionship and khalidin.
Denial of ayat and arrogance receive exclusion imagery and Jahannam as the final lodging.
Connects al-sayyi'at with fire companionship and khalidin; a secondary response-outcome parallel.
Names those who exchanged divine favor for kufr and led their people to ruin.
Names Jahannam as the destination completing the preceding kufr sequence.
Commands entry through Jahannam's gates with khalidin and identifies arrogance.
Gives a fire consequence that intensifies when it abates, extending the outcome imagery.
Makes Jahannam recompense for kufr and mockery of ayat and messengers.
Jahannam is marked by neither death nor life for one arriving as mujrim.
Links excess and disbelief in ayat to the more lasting final punishment.
Kuffar cannot repel fire from faces or backs, adding a direct fire boundary.
Opposition to ayat is joined to al-jahim companionship.
Denial of the Hour is paired with a prepared sa'ir, a secondary final-outcome route.
Explicitly states Jahannam encompasses al-kafirin.
Sets fire as the final return of al-fasiqun, with repeated return after attempted exit.
Identifies Jahannam as the promised destination in a direct address.
Makes prior kufr the stated basis for entering the preceding Jahannam.
Kuffar are driven in groups toward Jahannam, a close collective parallel.
Adds Jahannam's gates, khalidin, and arrogance to the preceding collective scene.
Denial of al-kitab and sent messages closely matches rejection after disclosed written evidence.
Completes the preceding denial route with fire entry imagery.
Fire is the dwelling whether or not those within endure; adds an outcome boundary.
Assigns Jahannam and an evil destination to those who kufaru bi-rabbihim.
Places al-qasitun as fuel for Jahannam, a secondary classification-and-fire parallel.
Saqar is assigned in a nearby condemnation sequence, but the focus categories are implicit.
Kufr in ayat defines the group of the left, a compact classification parallel.
Fire enclosing that group completes the preceding classification.
